A.title: Fall, slide, lying afraid
A.prompt: One single continuous shot, no cuts, no camera jump, no time jump. Photorealistic cinematic alpine footage, 16:9, 24 fps, natural overcast winter daylight, cool blue-grey grade with a restrained palette of snow white, deep navy and charcoal, subtle organic film grain. SUBJECT: preserve the man in the reference images exactly, the same face and light stubble, deep navy technical ski jacket with restrained orange zipper pulls, dark charcoal ski pants, matte black helmet with dark reflective goggles, dark gloves, black ski boots, black skis, dark ski poles, same age impression, same build, same kit throughout, no logo, no brand mark, no badge, no scar. PLACE: an authentic Altai ski slope in winter, soft ungroomed powder over a firm base, snow-dusted conifers at the edges, distant rocky ridgeline slightly out of focus, flat overcast sky. Camera is on the downhill front-quarter side of the skier, on the same side of the action axis for the entire shot; he travels from upper right toward lower left of frame. ACTION, one unbroken take: first he carves a controlled turn at moderate speed, knees flexed, hips angulated over the outside ski, edges biting, a thin plume of powder off the uphill ski; then without any cut the downhill ski loses grip, his knee collapses inward, hips drop back over the tails, shoulders rotate uphill, arms open outward for balance, pole tips lift off the snow, his face goes from concentration to alarm; then the skis swing flat and skid sideways across the fall line throwing a wide low fan of powder, his weight goes behind his heels and he topples backward onto his side and back in the deep soft snow with a soft powder burst, realistic falling weight, no acrobatics, no spin, no flight; then he slides a short distance and comes to rest, snow dust settling, fine crystals hanging in the air and drifting down-slope, one ski attached, the other lying flat nearby, one pole near his hand; finally he lies still, propped slightly on one elbow, looking up the slope with genuine fear and disbelief, wide eyes, quick shallow breathing, frightened and vulnerable but conscious and not gory. CAMERA: one continuous low front-quarter camera tracking with modest speed, drifting slightly closer as the fall happens, settling and holding on the frightened face at the end, smooth stabilized motion, no whip pan, no crash zoom, no handheld shaking. PHYSICS: believable edges, weight transfer, ski drag on soft snow, powder with mass and gravity, garments and helmet straps moving naturally.
